notes.text: Overall, the codebase is well-structured for its age. The router and response implementations are solid but show signs of organic growth (deprecated aliases, magic numbers, back-compat workarounds). The test suite is comprehensive but suffers from large file sizes. No critical security issues found in the excerpts. The 'insecure http:// endpoint' findings were false positives (regex patterns, not actual endpoints). The lack of a lockfile is a supply-chain risk. Recommend prioritizing: 1) add lockfile, 2) refactor test file organization, 3) address router sync limit configurability, 4) clean up deprecated internal utilities.

findings.title: Hardcoded synchronous iteration limit (100) in router handle
findings.description:
The router limits synchronous middleware/route processing to 100 iterations before yielding to the event loop. While this prevents stack overflow, the magic number is not configurable and could cause unexpected latency spikes for apps with many matching layers.

> Validation: cited 125-135 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 206-210; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Expose as a configurable option (e.g., `router.syncLimit`) with a sensible default, or use a more dynamic approach based on call stack depth.
findings.benefit: Allows tuning for high-throughput or deep-middleware applications; avoids arbitrary yield points.
findings.risk: Low — changing the limit could affect CPU fairness; needs benchmarking.

verification.note: cited 125-135 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 206-210; citation corrected

findings.title: matchLayer catches and returns errors as match results
findings.description: matchLayer catches exceptions from layer.match() and returns the error object. The caller treats non-boolean returns as `layerError`, which then gets passed to error handlers. This conflates matching failures (e.g., malformed regex) with route errors, potentially masking bugs.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish match errors from route errors: re-throw or wrap match errors in a distinct type, or log and treat as 500 rather than passing to route error handlers.
findings.benefit: Prevents matching bugs from being silently handled as application errors; improves debuggability.
findings.risk: Medium — could change error-handling behavior for edge cases; needs test coverage.

findings.title: No lockfile committed next to package.json
findings.description: Without a lockfile, every `npm install` resolves fresh versions — CI, teammates, and production can drift apart silently.
findings.suggestion: Commit the lockfile matching your package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and install with `npm ci` in CI.
findings.benefit: Identical dependency trees everywhere; fewer "works on my machine" failures.
findings.risk: None — adding a lockfile is additive.

modelVerdicts.reason: No package-lock.json or yarn.lock shown in repository summary; lockfile absence confirmed by static analysis.

findings.title: Trust proxy back-compat uses fragile symbol-like property
findings.description:
The code uses a string key `@@symbol:trust_proxy_default` on the settings object to track whether trust proxy was explicitly set, for inheritance behavior. This is a workaround for lack of real Symbols in older Node versions and is fragile (string collision possible).

findings.suggestion: Replace with a real Symbol (available since Node 4) or a WeakMap keyed by the app instance.
findings.benefit: Cleaner, collision-proof internal state tracking; modernizes codebase.
findings.risk: Very low — internal implementation detail with no public API impact.
